text: The Kalinago are an Indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles, islands in the Caribbean.
Kalinago is their own name, while Columbus and the Spanish called them Caribs.
src: The Kalinago, also known as the Island Caribs, are an Indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles / among the dominant peoples of the Caribbean
Kalinago (plural) and Karifuna (singular) are their own names; Carib, first recorded by Columbus, is an exonym

text: Their old stories say their ancestors came from South America about 800 years ago.
Scholars now think these newcomers joined the peoples already living on the islands.
src: The traditional account, almost as old as Columbus and widespread in oral testimony, held that the Kalinago came from South America, from the Orinoco around 1200 CE
the Kalinago appear from archaeology and ancient DNA to have formed from the islands’ own peoples together with newcomers from the mainland

text: The Kalinago are seafarers, and they travel and fish in dugout canoes made from trees.
Fish is still their main food, often cooked in one pot with yams and coconut cream.
src: Seafarers and warriors / Dugout canoes, made from trees such as Cedrela odorata ... they are still used for fishing and travel between the islands
Fish remains the core of their diet / the one pot of dasheen, yams, tannia and green bananas cooked with fresh fish or smoked meat in coconut cream

text: The Kalinago kept their freedom against Spain, but English and French settlers took their islands.
Almost 400 years ago, settlers killed about 2,000 Kalinago on the island of Saint Kitts.
src: In the Lesser Antilles the Kalinago held out / they kept their independence against Spain, France and England for generations / By 1640 those not enslaved had been forcibly removed to Dominica / by 1763 the British had annexed both
On Saint Kitts in 1626 English and French settlers massacred an estimated 2,000 Kalinago

text: On Saint Vincent, Kalinago and free West Africans formed a new people, the Garifuna.
The British later forced the Garifuna to leave, and today they live mainly in Central America.
src: On Saint Vincent, Kalinago and free West Africans formed the Garifuna
after the Second Carib War 4,338 Garifuna were deported to Roatan / The Garifuna, who share common ancestry with the Kalinago, live mainly in Central America

text: Today most Kalinago live in the Kalinago Territory, on the island of Dominica.
They elect their own chief, and some still build canoes in the traditional way.
src: today they live chiefly in the Kalinago Territory of Dominica / 3,700 acres on the east coast of Dominica
The Kalinago of Dominica elect their own chief / with renewed interest in making them in the traditional way
